dossier.public_summary: A dip near 14.9 days looks planet-sized and flat on average, but its depth jumps from about 1100 ppm to 4700 ppm between TESS sectors and between individual transits. That level of variability is not expected for a planet and points to stellar variability or a few bad transits rather than a real transit.

reasons.why: depth changes by sector (1116 ppm vs 4153 ppm vs 4700 ppm, depth_change_pct 107.9) on the all-sky check; sector_depths_by_source=changes_within_a_source with p_constant_all 5.340675965834079e-09, so sector depths differ even in the same SPOC product not a calibration offset
individual transits also inconsistent (chi2 46.28513342474475 dof 4), outliers at 5493 ppm sigma 4.1 and 1116 ppm in sector 18, share_of_top_3 0.935, so dip not due to a steady planet

no high-significance odd/even or secondary diagnostic, and shape flat-bottom favours planet, but cannot overcome 4-order-of-magnitude depth instability; neighbours plausible_within_1px 0 and contratio 0.01152 argue against NEB but on-target variability/false alarm best explanation
